name: Stored payment and address data
plain: Saved cards and addresses a browser, wallet or the site itself can fill at checkout.
meaning: Browser autofill fills a saved card only after the person picks it, and often asks for the CVC. Apple Pay and Google Pay give the merchant a tokenised card, not the card number. Sites that store cards keep tokens from a payment provider.

web.api: Payment Request API: new PaymentRequest(methods, details).show(); autocomplete tokens cc-number, shipping address

access.persistence: Saved in the browser profile or wallet until deleted; merchant tokens until revoked
access.revocation: Clear site data, browser privacy settings
steps: Site calls PaymentRequest.show from a click
Browser shows saved cards and addresses

data.metric: Card token, billing and shipping address

limits.headline: Can fill in saved cards and addresses at checkout, if you choose them
limits.user_action: You tap a field at checkout, pick a saved card or address, or tap a wallet button.
can: Fill your name, address and card from the browser, a wallet or the site
Offer a saved card from your account on that site
Fill a billing or shipping address in one tap
cannot: See all your saved cards without you choosing one
Fill your security code (CVC) without asking you in many browsers
Share your saved cards with other sites
Fill anything if you turned autofill off
limits.differs: Chrome and Safari fill saved cards and addresses. Firefox only fills addresses in many cases.

story.what_it_is: Saved cards and addresses can be filled in at checkout.

marketing.name: Payment and address form best practices
marketing.pitch: web.dev teaches how saved cards and addresses help people check out faster and make fewer errors.

story.for_you: Checkout forms fill your name, address and card in a tap. It saves time, but your data sits in your browser, wallet or the shop's account.
story.for_makers: Makers get faster checkouts and fewer typing mistakes, which lifts sales. Shops that keep cards on file also get easy repeat buying and subscription billing.

use_cases.example: Your saved address and card fill the form in one tap on a store.
A takeout app remembers your address and card for next time.
A booking site fills passenger info and your card.
A subscription site bills you every month from the saved card.
A skimmer script on a checkout page tries to read the filled fields.
A wallet app offers its saved cards across many shops.

technical_bounds: Merchant gets a device token (DPAN) with Apple Pay not the card number
Payment Request needs a user gesture and HTTPS
Autofill phishing: hidden fields can be filled after one click on a visible field

abuse: Harvesting hidden autofilled fields, card testing

history.change: Autofill phishing demo with hidden fields (Kuosmanen)
